How it was scored

  • Scanned with OpenSCAP in the image build on 2026-10-19 18:25 UTC.
  • Content: SCAP Security Guide 0.1.82, profile “DISA STIG for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10” (xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_profile_stig), with the refined value listed below.
  • Score = rules passed ÷ (rules passed + rules failed). Every rule listed under Exemptions failed in the scan and counts as a failure in the score. Not-applicable and not-checked rules are not scored.
  • The build's OpenSCAP gate was enforced: floor 90%, and no failing rule without a documented exemption.
  • FIPS mode is enabled, using the OS vendor's FIPS cryptographic modules.
  • Red Hat Enterprise Linux images are BYOL: you supply your own Red Hat subscription. StigReady does not sell or provide Red Hat commercial licenses.

An OpenSCAP score measures this image against SSG content. It is not a certification, authorization or accreditation, and it is not an assessment of your system.

Exemptions (12)

Each rule below fails in the image for the reason given, and the last column is what you do to meet it on your instance. The reasons and actions come from the build record (the signed POA&M lists the same rules).

RuleSTIG IDCategoryWhy it fails in the imageWhat you do
grub2_admin_username
Set the Boot Loader Admin Username to a Non-Default Value		—AWS Marketplace policy: you complete it after launchAWS Marketplace policy prohibits meeting this rule in an AMI: "AMI must not contain hardcoded secrets such as system user and service passwords (including hashed passwords)" and "Password-based authentication for instance services is prohibited. This applies even if the password is generated, reset, or defined by the user at launch"; Linux AMIs "must allow users to get fully privileged access (for example, to allow sudo access)" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/userguide/product-and-ami-policies.html). The rule needs a boot loader or root password hash in the image, or a sudo password for the key-only default user.After launch run `sudo stigready-set-credentials` (installed in the image): it sets your own GRUB superuser and password, root password and a sudo password for your admin user, and removes NOPASSWD, which meets this rule on your instance.

fapolicy_default_deny
Configure Fapolicy Module to Employ a Deny-all, Permit-by-exception Policy to Allow the Execution of Authorized Software Programs.		—Cloud usability: risk acceptedA default-deny fapolicyd allowlist blocks dnf, Ansible and every customer workload not in the list on a general-purpose image.Build an allowlist for your workloads, then set fapolicyd to deny-by-default.
network_configure_name_resolution
Configure Multiple DNS Servers in /etc/resolv.conf		—Cloud usability: risk acceptedThe rule wants two DNS servers in resolv.conf. On EC2 the VPC resolver is supplied by DHCP; the AMI owner manages DNS.Configure at least two name servers for your network, or keep the VPC resolver per your policy.
selinux_context_elevation_for_sudo
Elevate The SELinux Context When An Administrator Calls The Sudo Command		—Cloud usability: risk acceptedThe STIG's sudoers line (TYPE=sysadm_t ROLE=sysadm_r) makes sudo fail for the default unconfined_u login, so the image would have no working administrator.Map your admin users to staff_u/sysadm_u, then add the TYPE/ROLE sudoers line.
rsyslog_remote_loghost
Ensure Logs Sent To Remote Host		—Remote log offload: needs your log serverThese rules send logs to the customer's central log server. The address, certificates and transport are the customer's; there is no log host we could point the image at.Point rsyslog (with TLS), auditd remote logging and/or systemd-journal-upload at your log server, with your CA.
configure_opensc_card_drivers
Configure opensc Smart Card Drivers		—Smart card / CAC: needs your PKISmart card (CAC/PIV) login needs a card reader and the customer's own PKI: their CA certificates, OCSP/CRL endpoints and certificate-to-user mapping. A cloud instance has no reader, and no CA or mapping we could ship is correct for any customer. Some of these rules only install or enable a package; they are exempt with the class so the image does not run a smart card stack that cannot be used, and the customer enables it with their PKI.If you use CAC/PIV: install opensc and pcsc-lite, enable pcscd, install your CA bundle, and configure SSSD (or pam_pkcs11 on Ubuntu) certificate verification, OCSP/CRL and the certificate mapping for your directory.

CVE scan

This version's evidence has no CVE scan. The build's scanner (Trivy) does not cover Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10 packages, so its empty result for this image is not shown as a count: zero findings from it would not mean the image has no known CVEs.
